newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek government leaves settlement row to bourse.
newsitem.headline: Greek government leaves settlement row to bourse.

text.p: The Athens bourse must sort out settlement problems on its own and the government will not take any initiative in the row which prompted brokerages to boycott all trading on Friday, government spokesman Dimitris Reppas said.
"The stock exchange, on its own, will face this problem and everything will go well," Reppas told reporters at his routine daily briefing.

Asked if the government would guarantee settlement payments, he said: "The government cannot undertake initiatives which do not correspond to the legal framework (of the stock exchange). There are others who must assume their responsibilities."
When pressed to name those who should take charge, he said: "I've been very clear. Anyone else who guarantees".

Brokers have boycotted trading, effectively closing the bourse on Friday, saying the clearing house failed to pay some brokerages on Thursday. The clearing house has not commented on the brokers' statements.
The brokers said that they had boycotted trading to pressure the government into taking action to sort out the settlement row before it grew into a real crisis.
Stock exchange president Manolis Xanthakis has cut short his trip to Hong Kong to return to Athens in view of the settlement problem. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
